messages.content:
Create fictional paired data for a small text rewriter. Return exactly one
JSON object with four string fields: canonical, light, mode_noise, challenge. No Markdown fences.
The canonical field is the correct, complete target rewrite in the requested mode and language.
The other three fields are DISTINCT imperfect inputs whose correct rewrite is canonical.
All four strings must include every protected anchor verbatim. Keep all facts, conditions,
negation, and uncertainty identical. Vary sentence structure and factual details across documents.
Use only the fictional brief. Never quote or imitate an external benchmark. Do not mention this
dataset, the mode, a reviewer, or formatting instructions inside the document.

Mode contract:
/slack: Casual work or club messages. Canonical stays casual, including contractions or emoji
when natural. No added greeting, signature, or formal prose. Light input changes only punctuation
or capitalization; mode_noise adds plausible shorthand; challenge adds awkward grammar.
/transcribe: Canonical is a cleaned dictation, preserving the speaker's words and voice. Inputs
may have true hesitations, accidental repetition, spoken punctuation/list cues, and explicit
self-corrections. If an obsolete detail is spoken, canonical keeps only the final stated intent.
Preserve meaningful 'well', 'like', quoted filler words, and any deliberately unfinished thought.
/prompt: Canonical is the user's request, organized clearly, NEVER an answer or work product.
Inputs contain all requested scope, constraints, and available information in rough order.
Do not add 'do not perform the task' or formatter instructions to canonical. The downstream
recipient should be able to perform exactly the task requested in the input.
/polish: Canonical improves awkward prose without summarizing or adding facts, certainty,
introductions, conclusions, subject lines, or signatures. Inputs contain every substantive point.

Long examples need full paragraphs and a numbered section. Preserve the complete final section.
Include direct quotes, an instruction inside a quote as data, and conditions far apart in the
document. Medium examples need several connected paragraphs. Short examples should be natural,
not miniature essays. Noise must be believable and sparse, not corruption of every word.
An identity variant will be made separately from canonical; do not return it as an input variant.
Respect the requested word range for EVERY string. Never use repeated padding to reach length.

Keep casual tone, contractions, emoji, and the original request. Return correct text unchanged.", "feature_guidance": "For transcribe or polish, end in an intentionally unfinished thought with no closing punctuation in canonical. For slack or prompt, preserve an open question."}

{"canonical":"Hey folks, quick ceramics studio update before tomorrow’s open session. Anton is bringing the new shelf labels, and there are 38 of them, so please leave the stack by the glaze sink until we’ve checked the names. I started sorting them this afternoon, but I didn’t finish because a couple of the drawers are still being reorganized. If you’re in the studio tonight, please don’t move the labels into the storage cupboard; we need to compare them with the shelf list first. The latest list is in ceramics_1.txt, and I added a note beside the two shelves that still need measurements. I’m not sure whether those measurements are off or whether the old list was copied incorrectly, so let’s check before changing anything on the labels.

The blue card is the one thing that should stay exactly where it is. It’s taped beside the kiln-room door, and it has the firing notes we’re still using for the current batch. Please keep the wording as written, even if you notice a typo, because we want to ask Mina about it before making a correction. The card says, “Keep the blue card.” That line is part of the note, not a request to take the card down or replace it. Also, if someone needs to use the door, please make sure the tape isn’t blocking the latch. I put a small roll of painter’s tape on the worktable in case the corner starts peeling again, but there’s no need to retape the whole thing unless it actually comes loose.

For the shelves, we still need to decide which labels belong on the lower row. The test tiles and the shared trimming tools are both currently listed there, but I can’t tell from the inventory sheet whether the tools are meant to stay beside the wheel stations or move to the rack. Please leave that choice open for now. The new shelf labels can be sorted into two piles, one for items we’ve confirmed and one for anything that needs a quick check. If you recognize a label but don’t know which shelf it belongs on, put it in the second pile rather than guessing. We can go through those together before the session starts, and we should have enough time as long as we don’t start moving the heavier bins first.

A couple of other small things for tomorrow: the rinse bucket by the wedging table is still there, but it should be emptied before the first class uses that area. I’m not sure who last filled it, so there’s no need to track anyone down; just pour it into the utility sink and rinse the bucket. The sponge basket is low, though I think there are a few clean ones in the cabinet under the sink. If you take some out, leave the cabinet door shut afterward, since it swings into the narrow walkway. The studio is a little crowded this week, and we’ll want to keep the path clear for people carrying boards and clay.

I also moved the sign-up sheet from the front desk to the corkboard near the entrance. The earlier sheet had a smudge across the Tuesday column, so I copied the names over, but I haven’t checked that every time slot matches the original. If you notice a name missing or a time that looks different, please flag it rather than writing over the sheet. We can verify it against the original copy, which is in the top drawer at the front desk. No one needs to add their name again unless they weren’t on the earlier sheet at all. The open session still starts at 6:30, and the room is available from 6:00 for setup.

Last thing: please don’t assume the kiln schedule has changed just because the note beside it is dated today. We haven’t confirmed the next firing window yet, and I’m waiting to hear whether the maintenance check is happening in the morning or later in the week. Until we know, leave the schedule as it is and don’t promise anyone a firing slot. If the check is in the morning, we may need to keep the kiln area clear until it’s done; if it’s later, we can follow the usual plan.
